entries.title: Name participant roles in each of your event's languages
entries.summary: On a multi-language event, every participant role, including the ones your team created, has **Language variants**: a singular and plural name for each language. Reviewers, submitters and speakers who pick that language see it on the Review portal (cards, **Print all**, the submission page), in the submission form's participant roles and on the speaker portal's Participants tab. A language left blank shows the role's own name.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Roles → ⋯ Edit → Language variants

entries.use_case: An association running its review in Spanish and French can show “Autor presentador” and “Coautor” to Spanish reviewers instead of the English role names.

cs_action.note: Nothing switches on by itself: role names have to be typed per language in Program → Settings → Roles. For a multi-language customer whose reviewers see English role chips, walk them through adding the names for their custom roles. Track names are set separately, on the Track field's Language variants.

internal.gotchas: Shows only on events with more than one language. Track names are not edited here; they are option translations on the Track field. Speaker, Chairperson and Moderator already read in Spanish, French and German while they keep their original names; a role's own variant overrides that.
internal.staff_path: Program → Settings → Roles → ⋯ Edit → Language variants (event must have more than one language under Settings → Event Details → Supported Languages)
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers and speakers now see your own role names, like Presenting author and Co-author, in their language.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A multi-language customer reports role names (Presenting author, Co-author, …) in English in the Review portal, the submission form or the speaker portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with more than one event language, especially medical and scientific societies reviewing abstracts in several languages.

entries.title: Awards and Interest Form videos stream, and file questions take drag and drop
entries.summary: File questions on Awards nomination forms and Interest Forms (session and speaker questions, signed in or not) now upload straight to Sessionboard: drag a file onto the box or choose one, up to 5 GB. A video entry gets a copy made for streaming (up to 720p) a minute or two after upload, so reviewers in Awards review and the Review portal watch it without long pauses; **Download** always gives the original. Files your team adds from the submission sheet work the same way.

where.path: Awards → program → Submissions → open an entry → click a video (or the reviewer's portal → My Reviews → open an entry)

entries.use_case: An awards program that collects video entries can let reviewers watch them straight through instead of waiting for a large original to buffer.

cs_action.note: Automatic for files uploaded after this release. Entries uploaded before keep playing and downloading as they were (they are on Filestack's CDN and cannot get a streaming copy). HTML and SVG uploads are refused; prod had none on Awards or Interest Forms.

internal.gotchas: A video opened within a minute or two of upload may still play the original while its copy is made. Light videos that already stream well play as uploaded, with no note. The upload limit is 5 GB a file.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Submissions → open an entry with a video → click the video
internal.talk_track: Video entries now stream for your reviewers, and Download still gives the full-quality original.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer launching a video entry category, or reporting Awards reviewers seeing videos pause or load slowly.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with video categories, and Interest Form customers who collect sizzle reels or session videos.

entries.title: Learning Sites: buy a course by card, play SCORM/xAPI/cmi5 packages, and track progress; Awards Sites: People's Choice voting, native file uploads, and nomination improvements
entries.summary: **Learning Sites** now let learners purchase a priced course by credit card through the organizer's payment gateway (member pricing and coupons apply), play SCORM, xAPI and cmi5 course packages inside lessons, view interactive blocks (labeled graphics, processes, timelines, branching scenarios), claim credit certificates from **My certificates**, and see completed courses in **My progress**. Timed quizzes retain their result, and written-answer quizzes show a "You can retake once it's scored" notice while scoring is pending. **Awards Sites** now show a **Vote** button on People's Choice ballots, accept file-question uploads natively (no third-party uploader), display a **Nominate someone** link on the open-programs list, use "nomination" wording throughout, and show each program's description on the open list. Reviewer scorecards label their controls, reviewers see answers on section-free forms, and the scoring form scrolls correctly on phones. Registration and event-page chrome is now available in English, Spanish, French and German; the public floor map is translated into German, Spanish and French; and the Site builder canvas renders in the admin's own language.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Learning Commerce and/or Awards People's Choice; then configure priced courses or People's Choice programs in your site settings

where.path: Learning Site → course page → Buy; Awards Site → open programs list → Vote / Nominate someone

entries.use_case: Organizations that sell professional-development courses can now charge learners directly on their Learning Site using their own payment gateway, with member pricing and coupons, without any custom checkout integration. Awards programs running a People's Choice round can let the public vote with a single button, and nominators can upload supporting files without a third-party uploader.

cs_action.note: Card checkout appears only on courses an admin has priced above $0 on an org with a connected gateway. SCORM/xAPI/cmi5 packages require LEARNING_PACKAGES_CONTENT_HOST and LEARNING_PACKAGES_BUCKET to point at a dedicated non-sessionboard.com content domain — not yet set in production. Awards People's Choice and native file uploads are live for Awards Sites. Self-serve sign-ups remain off by default (LEARNING_SIGNUP_ENABLED=false).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about selling courses on their Learning Site, running a People's Choice vote on their Awards Site, or accepting file uploads from nominees without Filestack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers who want to monetize courses; Awards customers running a People's Choice round or collecting file evidence from nominees.
internal.staff_path: Learning Site admin → course settings → Price; Awards Site admin → program settings → People's Choice / file questions
internal.gotchas: SCORM/xAPI/cmi5 package playback is gated behind an env variable not yet set in production — do not promise it to customers until the content domain is configured. Card checkout only appears when the org has a connected gateway and the course has a price > $0.
internal.talk_track: Your Learning Site can now sell courses directly — learners pay by card, get access immediately, and track their certificates in one place. On Awards, the public can vote with one click and nominees can upload files without any third-party tool.

draft.docs_gap: The sell-courses guide should add a section on the learner-facing buy card (member pricing, coupon entry, and the back link), and the course-packages guide should note the SCORM/xAPI/cmi5 content-domain prerequisite. The awards winners guide should document the People's Choice Vote button and the native file-upload flow for nomination forms.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Learning gives you a branded site where learners sign in, buy courses, work through SCORM or native content, and earn certificates — all in one place. You set the price, connect your payment gateway, and choose which courses require purchase; learners see their progress and certificates in a personal dashboard. Use it to monetize continuing-education content, onboard members, or deliver compliance training without stitching together a separate LMS and storefront.

entries.title: Public ballots no longer expose nominee email addresses, phone numbers, or hidden questions
entries.summary: Email addresses and phone numbers are now stripped from public Awards ballots and anonymous evaluation ballots before they reach the viewer. On Awards ballots, questions marked as hidden in the round's **Hidden Questions** setting are also suppressed. Signed-in voters on evaluation ballots continue to see any contact fields the admin explicitly allow-listed.
entries.use_case: Organizations running public Awards ballots or open evaluation votes can be confident that nominee and nominator contact details are never leaked to anonymous visitors, even when those fields appear on the submission form.

cs_action.note: This is a security fix shipped urgently. At the time of the prod investigation there were 0 public-vote Awards rounds in Prod US and EU, so no Awards ballot was actively exposed. Three evaluation public rounds in Prod US had an email or phone field in their allow-list by admin choice — those fields are now hidden for anonymous viewers but still visible to signed-in voters. Reach out to those three accounts if they notice the change.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why an email or phone field they added to their nomination form is no longer visible on the public ballot, or why a hidden question is no longer showing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using public-vote Awards rounds or public evaluation ballots where the submission form includes email or phone fields.
internal.gotchas: The fix is applied server-side and is retroactive — no action needed by admins. Signed-in voters on evaluation rounds still see allow-listed contact fields as before. The ballot card list (submission_card_field_ids) is unchanged.
internal.talk_track: To protect nominee privacy, email and phone answers are now automatically removed from public ballots. Hidden questions set in the round editor are also respected. Signed-in reviewers on evaluation rounds still see any contact fields you explicitly allow-listed.

draft.docs_gap: The ballot guide should note that email and phone fields are always redacted for anonymous viewers, and that Awards round hidden questions are enforced on the public ballot detail view.

entries.title: Self-nomination submissions no longer show applicant details twice
entries.summary: In Awards programs using **Nomination mode: Self-nomination**, the applicant's name and email previously appeared under both **About you** and the **Nominee** section in the submission detail view. Mirrored nominee fields are now hidden when the same answer is already shown in the submitter section, so each piece of information appears exactly once. Reviewers on the Site and admins in the **Awards submission sidebar** both see the corrected layout. Non-mirrored nominee fields (such as a headshot) and "Nominate others" programs are unchanged.

where.path: Awards → [Program] → Submissions → [Submission] (admin sidebar and reviewer Site detail)

entries.use_case: Organizers running self-nomination awards programs can now share the submission detail view with reviewers without confusion — each piece of applicant information appears once, making scorecards easier to read and reducing reviewer questions about duplicate fields.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that applicant name or email shows up twice in a self-nomination submission detail, or a reviewer is confused by duplicate Nominee fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running an Awards program with Nomination mode set to Self-nomination.
internal.staff_path: Awards → [Program] → Submissions → open any submission → check the sidebar or reviewer Site detail
internal.gotchas: Only mirrored fields (where the nominee answer is identical to the submitter answer) are hidden. Fields with no submitter twin (e.g. nominee headshot), fields with an admin-only twin, and fields whose value differs from the submitter twin are still shown. Exports, merge tags, gallery/winners, and field_values are unaffected — nominee columns remain populated.
internal.talk_track: In self-nomination programs the platform used to copy the applicant's details into both the 'About you' and 'Nominee' sections of the detail view; now each answer appears only once, so reviewers see a clean, unambiguous form.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that in Self-nomination programs, mirrored nominee fields are automatically hidden from the submission detail view (admin sidebar and reviewer Site) to avoid showing the same answer twice, while non-mirrored fields such as headshotsremain visible.

entries.title: Reviewer scoring form scrolls naturally on phones
entries.summary: On phones (375 px and narrower), the reviewer submission page — for both Awards reviews and session evaluation rounds — now scrolls as one continuous page. The header, back link, previous/next controls, and the **"You have already reviewed this submission"** banner scroll away with the form, so the full scoring form and **Save** button are always reachable. On evaluation rounds, the section-jump pill row stays pinned at the top, and tabbing through scoring fields keeps the focused field visible below it.

where.path: Reviews → round → entry (Awards) or Evaluations → round → entry (Sessions)

entries.use_case: Reviewers scoring submissions on a phone could previously only see a small portion of the form at a time because the header was pinned and the content scrolled inside a tiny box. Now the whole page scrolls naturally, so reviewers can complete and save a scorecard without fighting the layout on a small screen.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A reviewer reports that the scoring form is hard to use on a phone, or an organizer says reviewers are struggling to complete reviews on mobile.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using Awards review rounds or session evaluation plans where reviewers are likely to score on a phone.
internal.staff_path: Reviews → round → entry (Awards) or Evaluations → round → entry (Sessions) — view at 375 px
internal.gotchas: Desktop behaviour (≥1024 px) is unchanged: the header stays fixed and the two columns scroll independently. Focus mode is also unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers can now score submissions on their phone without fighting a tiny scroll box — the whole page scrolls naturally and the Save button is always reachable.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the scoring form is fully usable on phones, including how the section-jump pill row stays pinned on evaluation rounds and how keyboard focus is kept clear of it.
draft.why_use_it: The reviewer scoring form lets judges evaluate and score submitted proposals or award nominations from any device. Reviewers can read the full submission, fill in scoring questions, leave comments, and submit their scorecard — all from a single page. The section-jump pill row on evaluation rounds lets reviewers move quickly between the submission details and each scoring section without losing their place.

entries.title: Awards form builder sections and questions load in their saved order
entries.summary: Sections and questions in the **Form Builder** now always appear in the order they were saved. Previously, a database query without an explicit sort could return sections and questions in an unpredictable order on reload.
entries.use_case: An organizer who has carefully ordered their nomination form sections (e.g. "About you" before "Your nomination") can trust that order is preserved every time the form builder loads, without needing to re-sort after each session.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their awards form sections or questions appear in the wrong order after saving or reloading the form builder.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Platform Awards with a multi-section submission form.
internal.gotchas: The fix applies to the Platform Awards form builder read endpoint. The self-serve Awards form reader and the reviewer read-only form were already ordering correctly and are unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Sections and questions in the awards form builder now reliably load in the order you saved them — no more unexpected reshuffling on reload.
